title: Passé récent: venir de
goal: By the end of this lesson you can say that something has just happened with venir de + infinitive, in the present and in the past, and recognise the Quebec 'j'viens juste de'.

learn.h: Venir de + infinitive = to have just done
body: To say that something happened a moment ago, French uses *venir* in the present + *de* + infinitive: *Je viens de manger* (I have just eaten), *Le bus vient de partir* (The bus has just left).
This is the mirror image of the futur proche: *Je vais manger* (I'm about to eat) / *Je viens de manger* (I've just eaten).
*De* becomes *d'* before a vowel or silent h: *Elle vient d'arriver*, *Ils viennent d'acheter une maison*.

head: Person
venir (present)
Example
rows: Vous venez de rater le bus.

learn.tip: aller + infinitive = about to happen; venir de + infinitive = just happened.

learn.h: Venir de in the past: venais de
body: To say what had just happened at a moment in the past, put *venir* in the imparfait: *Je venais de rentrer quand le téléphone a sonné* (I had just come home when the phone rang).
Never use the passé composé of venir for this meaning: *Je suis venu de manger* is wrong.

Object pronouns go before the infinitive, not before *venir*: *Je viens de le voir* (I just saw him), *Elle vient de lui parler* (She just talked to him), *On vient d'en acheter* (We just bought some).
Negation surrounds *venir*: *Il ne vient pas de partir, il est parti il y a une heure.* In practice, the negative is rare; people say *Il n'est pas parti depuis longtemps*.

learn.h: Don't confuse it with 'to come from'
body: *Venir de* + a place means 'to come from': *Je viens de Toronto* (I'm from Toronto). *Venir de* + an infinitive means 'to have just': *Je viens de téléphoner*.
Juste, tout juste and à l'instant can add emphasis: *Il vient juste de partir*, *Elle vient tout juste d'arriver*, *Je viens de le voir à l'instant*.

examples.en: We had just had supper when they arrived.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu viens de dire?

quebec.intro: In Quebec speech, 'je viens de' is shortened to 'j'viens d'' and almost always reinforced with 'juste': 'j'viens juste de finir'. Be careful: Quebecers also have 'être après + infinitive', which means 'to be in the middle of doing', not 'to have just done'.

items.note: juste is very frequent in Quebec

items.std: Je suis en train de manger.
items.note: Informal Quebec: être après = in the middle of; NOT 'I just ate'

drills.q: How do you say 'I had just arrived'?
drills.why: Use the imparfait of venir for the past.

drills.q: Where does the pronoun go? 'She just called me.'

drills.why: être après + infinitive = to be in the middle of doing.

pron.tip: eel VYENN: the plural is not nasal.
Quebec: zhvyan zhust duh, often zhvyan zhus' d'.

dialogue.fr: Allô, est-ce que Marc est là?
Ah, tu viens juste de le manquer. Il vient de partir au gym.
dialogue.en: Ah, you just missed him. He just left for the gym.
Darn! Does he have his cell phone?

dialogue.fr: Non, je viens de le voir sur la table.
dialogue.en: No, I just saw it on the table.

dialogue.fr: Bon. Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu fais?
dialogue.en: OK. And you, what are you doing?

dialogue.fr: Je viens de rentrer du travail. Je venais d'enlever mes bottes quand le téléphone a sonné!
dialogue.en: I just got home from work. I had just taken my boots off when the phone rang!

dialogue.fr: Désolé! Peux-tu lui dire de me rappeler?
dialogue.en: Sorry! Can you tell him to call me back?

dialogue.fr: Pas de problème, je lui laisse un message.
dialogue.en: No problem, I'll leave him a message.

questions.q: Why can't A call Marc on his cell?
What had B just done when the phone rang?

speak.prompt: Say three things you have just done today with venir de.
speak.model: Je viens de déjeuner, je viens de lire mes courriels et je viens de faire du café.

speak.prompt: Say what you had just done when something happened (venais de + passé composé).
speak.model: Je venais de sortir quand il a commencé à neiger.

speak.prompt: Say 'He just left' in standard French, then the casual Quebec way.
speak.model: Il vient de partir. / Y vient juste de partir.

write.prompt: Write a text message (4–5 sentences) to a friend describing what you have just done and what you are about to do. Use venir de and aller + infinitive.
write.model: Salut! Je viens de finir mon cours de français. Je viens aussi de passer à l'épicerie. Là, je vais faire le souper. Après, on va regarder le match avec mes colocs. Tu viens?

quiz.q: 'Je vais partir' vs 'Je viens de partir': which is the recent past?
quiz.why: venir de = just happened; aller = about to happen.

options: I just came back from Calgary
quiz.why: venir de + place = to come from.

quiz.q: Which is correct for 'We had just left'?

options: a little while ago or soon
quiz.why: It refers to a moment close to now, past or future.

options: casual Quebec for 'Je viens de finir'
quiz.why: Quebec speech shortens je and adds juste.
